title: Operator-override acceptance record v1.0.0
description: `<run>/accepted.json` written by `python -m workflow accept <run> --candidate <sha> --reason "<text>" --by operator` (docs/PRD_ACCEPT_OVERRIDE.md; decisions.md [L8]): the operator's record that a blocked or abandoned run's candidate was merged by hand, and why. Written once, under the run's controller lock, validated with `workflow.verification.validate_schema("accepted", ...)` before the write, and never rewritten. Export 1.12.0 carries this object verbatim as the top-level `accepted` key (null for a run without one; the export fails, naming the file, when accepted.json does not validate). This schema and the viewer's `accepted` field (contracts/projects, z.strictObject with `via` optional) parse exactly this key set and nothing else. `candidate` is the run's own candidate commit (brief.candidate_commit), a full 40-hex sha. `reason` and `by` are required non-empty strings and `accepted_at` is a required UTC ISO date-time ending in `Z` (what `checks.now()` writes; `pattern` enforces it so a hand-edited non-ISO value fails the export the way the viewer's strict `z.iso.datetime()` would, [L14]); `by` is always "operator" (accept is operator-only); `via` is present only when the command ran from a Claude Code session (actor_record adds "claude-code"). `on_main` says whether the candidate is an ancestor of the target's main/master/base branch (never fetched). `review` is "recorded" when the run has a review.json, else "none". `open_findings` is every finding open at acceptance (decisions.md [L5]): the blocking P0/P1 (not resolved, accepted ones included) then the P2s whose disposition is `open`; `title` is the review finding's message verbatim and `lane` is its `worker` when that is a lane id, else null.
